answer: Allocate reward weight by short random walks from a fixed set of trusted roots, dividing each node's outgoing probability among its endorsed neighbors. A willow market with ten links into a fake cluster sends only limited probability across that cut; adding a thousand clones merely splits its landing mass. A farm must forge endorsements from outside its shale of aliases to gain weight, paying independent incumbents rather than minting free votes. Cap each root's total probability at one.
